faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Common questions, clear answers.
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about working with GreenAlgorithm.

q1.question: How long does a typical project take?
q1.answer: It varies by complexity. A simple website can take 2-4 weeks, a mobile app 2-4 months, and a full SaaS platform 4-6 months. We provide a detailed timeline during the discovery phase.

q2.question: Do you offer post-launch support?
q2.answer: Yes. We offer several maintenance packages that include security updates, bug fixes, 24/7 monitoring, and minor feature additions. Our team is available to ensure your software runs smoothly.

q3.question: Do I own the code?
q3.answer: Absolutely. Once the project is paid for, you own 100% of the source code and intellectual property. We deliver all code, documentation, and assets upon handoff.

q4.question: What technologies do you use?
q4.answer: We're stack-agnostic but specialize in modern tools: React, Next.js, Node.js, Python, Flutter, Go, and more. We choose the best technology for each project based on specific requirements.

q5.question: What is the work process like?
q5.answer: We follow an agile methodology with 4 phases: Discovery (understand your business), Design (create the visual experience), Development (build the product in 2-week sprints), and Launch (deployment with dedicated support).

q6.question: Can you work with my existing team?
q6.answer: Yes. We integrate seamlessly with existing teams using tools like Slack, Jira, GitHub, and daily standups. We can act as an extension of your team or lead the project entirely.

q7.question: What is the typical budget range?
q7.answer: Projects range from $5,000 USD for landing pages and MVPs to $100,000+ USD for complex enterprise platforms. We provide a detailed, transparent budget after the free discovery phase.

q8.question: Do you work with startups or only enterprises?
q8.answer: We work with both. From early-stage startups needing an MVP to established companies seeking digital transformation. We adapt our process and budget to each client's size and needs.

cybersecurity1.title: Protect your business: 10 cybersecurity threats in 2025
cybersecurity1.excerpt: Cyber threats are constantly evolving. Learn the 10 most critical threats businesses face this year and how to protect yourself.
cybersecurity1.content: From ransomware attacks to sophisticated AI-powered phishing, cyber threats are more complex than ever. In this article we analyze the most dangerous trends of 2025, including supply chain attacks, deepfakes for corporate deception, and cloud infrastructure vulnerabilities. We also cover proactive defense strategies: Zero Trust implementation, 24/7 AI monitoring, and incident response plans.

ai1.title: Generative AI in enterprise: A practical implementation guide
ai1.excerpt: How to integrate generative AI models into business processes securely, efficiently, and with measurable ROI.
ai1.content: Generative AI is transforming how businesses operate. From customer service automation with intelligent chatbots to content generation and predictive analytics. In this guide we cover: model selection (GPT, Claude, Llama), fine-tuning for specific cases, RAG architectures for enterprise data, and security and privacy best practices. We include real implementation cases with ROI metrics.

dev1.title: Next.js 15 vs pure React: When to choose each
dev1.excerpt: We analyze the advantages and disadvantages of Next.js vs pure React for different types of enterprise projects.
dev1.content: Choosing the right framework can make or break a project. Next.js 15 brings Server Components, streaming, and significant performance improvements. But it's not always the best option. We analyze when to use Next.js (e-commerce, SaaS, SEO-critical sites) vs pure React with Vite (internal dashboards, single-page apps, rapid prototypes). We include performance benchmarks, development complexity, and infrastructure costs.

cybersecurity2.title: Zero Trust Architecture: Step-by-step implementation
cybersecurity2.excerpt: Complete guide to migrating your infrastructure to a Zero Trust model without disrupting business operations.
cybersecurity2.content: The traditional perimeter security model is no longer enough. Zero Trust assumes no connection is secure by default, verifying every access in real time. We cover the 5 implementation phases: current access audit, network segmentation, multi-factor authentication, micro-segmentation, and continuous monitoring. We include recommended tools and time estimates for businesses of different sizes.

ai2.title: Intelligent automation: How n8n and AI transform operations
ai2.excerpt: Discover how to combine automated workflows with artificial intelligence to eliminate repetitive tasks and reduce errors.
ai2.content: The combination of n8n with AI models opens a world of possibilities for business automation. From automatic document processing to intelligent email classification and personalized report generation. We show 5 real workflows we implemented for clients: onboarding automation, invoice processing with OCR + AI, social media monitoring with sentiment analysis, and intelligent CRM synchronization.

dev2.title: Flutter 4.0: The future of cross-platform development
dev2.excerpt: We analyze the new features of Flutter 4.0 and why it's the best option for enterprise apps in 2025.
dev2.content: Flutter 4.0 introduces significant performance improvements, new native capabilities, and better platform integration. We analyze the new on-device AI APIs, Impeller rendering engine improvements, better macOS and Windows support, and new testing tools. We compare Flutter with React Native and Kotlin Multiplatform in terms of productivity, performance, and ecosystem for enterprise projects.

cybersecurity3.title: Ransomware in 2025: How to protect your critical infrastructure
cybersecurity3.excerpt: Ransomware attacks are more sophisticated than ever. We analyze new attacker tactics and the most effective defense strategies.
cybersecurity3.content: Ransomware has evolved from simple encryption to triple extortion operations: encryption, data leak threats, and simultaneous DDoS attacks. We analyze new variants like BlackCat and LockBit 4.0, their main entry vectors (vulnerable VPNs, exposed RDP, AI-powered phishing), and the multi-layered defense strategies every company must implement: immutable backups, network segmentation, AI-powered EDR, and tested response plans.

ai3.title: RAG vs Fine-tuning: When to use each approach for your enterprise chatbot
ai3.excerpt: Not all AI chatbots are the same. Discover when to use Retrieval-Augmented Generation versus direct fine-tuning.
ai3.content: Building an intelligent enterprise chatbot requires choosing the right architecture. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is ideal when you need answers based on up-to-date documents and a dynamic knowledge base. Fine-tuning shines when you need a specific response style or highly specialized domain. We compare costs, latency, accuracy, and real use cases: customer service, technical support, legal assistant, and financial analysis. Includes reference architecture with LangChain and LlamaIndex.

dev3.title: Go vs Rust vs Node.js: The definitive backend for startups in 2025
dev3.excerpt: We compare the three most popular backends for startups: performance, productivity, ecosystem, and development cost.
dev3.content: Choosing the right backend language is critical for a startup. Go offers native concurrency and simple deployment (single binary). Rust delivers maximum performance and memory safety without garbage collector. Node.js dominates in npm ecosystem and development speed. We do real benchmarks: HTTP throughput, API latency, memory consumption, and development time for common features (auth, CRUD, websockets, queues). Includes recommendations by startup type and budget.

cybersecurity4.title: AI-automated security audits: The new era
cybersecurity4.excerpt: AI is transforming security audits. Discover how to automate vulnerability detection and reduce response times.
cybersecurity4.content: Traditional security audits take weeks. With AI, we can scan entire codebases in hours identifying vulnerability patterns that human analysts would overlook. We cover tools like Snyk with AI, SonarQube with machine learning, and custom solutions with LLMs for code analysis. We show how to implement a CI/CD pipeline with automatic security scanning, report generation, and intelligent fix prioritization based on real risk.

ai4.title: Autonomous AI agents: Building systems that think for themselves
ai4.excerpt: AI agents are revolutionizing automation. Learn to build autonomous agents with tools, memory, and planning capabilities.
ai4.content: Beyond chatbots, AI agents can execute complex tasks autonomously: web research, API usage, code writing and execution, and decision-making based on objectives. We cover frameworks like CrewAI, AutoGen, and LangGraph. We show 3 real implementations: market research agent, level 2 technical support agent, and data analysis agent with report generation. We discuss current limitations, security best practices, and costs.

dev4.title: PostgreSQL vs MongoDB vs Redis: The definitive database guide for 2025
dev4.excerpt: Choosing the right database can define your project's success. We compare the most popular options with real use cases.
dev4.content: The database is the foundation of every application. PostgreSQL dominates in relational data with JSON support, full-text search, and extensions like pgvector for AI. MongoDB is ideal for flexible documents and rapid prototyping. Redis shines as cache, session store, and real-time. We analyze when to use each, hybrid usage patterns (PostgreSQL + Redis, MongoDB + PostgreSQL), migrations between them, and infrastructure costs on AWS and GCP. Includes performance benchmarks for CRUD operations, complex queries, and aggregations.
